_comment: Issue #179, the part of the rename an INSTALLATION project has to do.
Run this against the installation, with -Project, BEFORE syncing blocks. Until
it has run, the installation still holds the shared objects under their old
names, so a sync import with -ImportConflict replace matches nothing and files
a second copy of every block beside the old one.
Everything here is either shared code, or named by shared code:
- the 10 objects are the reference's own types and blocks, which live in the
installation as copies and are replaced by the sync.
- MqttVariables is the installation's GVL, but 20 shared blocks name it -
FB_MQTT_BASE declares STRING(GVL_MQTT.MQTT_TOPIC_LEN) and the self-wiring
prologue reaches into GVL_MQTT.fbMqttPublishQueue - so it has to follow or
every synced block fails with Identifier 'GVL_MQTT' not defined. Its
MEMBERS keep their names; only the list is renamed. "all": true because a
project with two controllers has two of them and both are compiled.
NOT here, on purpose - these are the installation's own and renaming them
changes what its PLC does rather than what it compiles against:
- PLC_PRG_* programs. Renaming one changes every persistent instance path
under it, so the building's retained state resets.
- PersistentVars, RS485Variables, DMXVariables, DALIVariables. No shared
block names them.
- instance names. They are the Home Assistant entity ids.
An owner who wants those too should start from 179-objects.json instead and
read docs/NamingConventionMigration.md first.
Objects the installation does not have are simply reported as absent, so this
map is safe to run against any installation regardless of which subsystems it
uses - trim the ones it reports missing if you prefer a silent run.
